turns.prompt: when I end a meeting, the recap leaves out any task that has a person on it but no deadline. like if they say 'Priya will send the contract' with no date it just isnt in the action items. can you fix it
turns.final_message:
I've changed the recap prompts so they keep tasks that have a person but no deadline. I haven't run a meeting to check it, so I can't confirm the model's output yet.

**Cause:** Nothing in the code throws these tasks away. The problem was the instructions given to the AI when a meeting ends. Most of the other prompts in the app already say "keep every action item that has an owner, even if it has no due date." The two used for the end-of-meeting recap didn't. And the Groq prompt's only example was a task with a date ("Bob: Draft invite copy by Wednesday"), which nudged the model to leave out undated ones.

**What I changed:**
- `electron/MeetingPersistence.ts:144`: added the rule to the shared recap rules. That covers both the default recap and the recaps for each mode, like Team Meet. "Priya will send the contract" should now come out as `Priya: Send the contract (no date given)`, and the model is told not to make up a date.
- `electron/llm/prompts.ts`: added the same rule to the Groq recap prompt, which is used when Groq is the provider.

**To check it:** run a short meeting where someone says something like "Priya will send the contract" with no date, end it, and see whether it shows up under action items.

**A separate bug I found and didn't fix:** the Groq prompt tells the model to return the overview under the name `"summary"`, but the code that saves the recap looks for `"overview"` and never reads `"summary"`. So the overview at the top of the recap is probably blank when Groq writes it. It's a small fix if you want me to make it.

I found and fixed three more places where these tasks were getting lost. I couldn't build or type-check, though: the project's packages aren't installed and downloading them was blocked. I also can't run a real meeting from here, so none of this is tested yet.

The database and the meeting screen show every action item the AI returns, so the loss happens before that, in what the AI is given and told:

1. **The meeting modes only asked for your own tasks.** Team Meet and Sales describe the Action Items section as "action items that were said **I** would do", and Recruiting says "that **I** have to do". The rule I added last time only covered the plain recap with no mode. With a mode on, the AI was correctly leaving out "Priya will send the contract" because Priya isn't you. The mode recap now includes everyone's tasks, written as `Owner: task (no date given)` when there's no date, even where the section description says "I". I changed the instructions rather than your saved mode settings, so your settings stay as they are.

2. **The end of longer meetings was cut off.** The recap only sent the AI the first 10,000 characters of the transcript, roughly the first 10–15 minutes. Tasks usually get handed out at the end, so they never reached the AI. It now keeps the opening and gives most of the space to the ending (`electron/MeetingPersistence.ts`). The total length sent is unchanged.

3. **Very long meetings get older parts condensed into short summaries,** and those summaries only kept topics, decisions and questions, not tasks. They now keep tasks with their owners too (`electron/SessionTracker.ts`).

**To test:** pick a mode (Team Meet is the clearest case). Near the end of a meeting longer than about 15 minutes, have someone say "Priya will send the contract" with no date. End the meeting and check the Action Items section.

If it still drops the task, tell me which mode you were in and whether the meeting was short or long. The next step would be a check after the AI answers that scans the transcript for "X will…" lines and adds any task the AI missed, so the result no longer depends on the AI following instructions.

The overview bug from last time is still unfixed: with Groq, the overview at the top of the recap is probably blank.

I've added a code check that runs after the AI writes the recap. It scans the transcript for tasks the AI left out and adds them to Action Items. It doesn't depend on the AI following instructions, which my last two changes did.

**What it catches** (new file `electron/utils/actionItemExtractor.ts`):
- "Priya will send the contract", "Tom is going to update the deck", "Raj needs to get the numbers"
- "Sam, can you share the notes?"
- "I'll follow up with legal" when you say it (it shows as `Me: …`)

**How it adds them:** a task with no date is written as `Priya: Send the contract (no date given)`. If the AI already listed a task, it isn't added twice, and nothing the AI wrote is removed or changed. With a mode on, the tasks go into that mode's Action Items section. It also runs when the AI call fails completely, so you still get these tasks.

**What I tested:** I ran it on sample transcript lines and it picked up all five tasks, dated and undated. It correctly skipped filler like "It will probably rain", "That will take time" and "I'll be honest", and it didn't repeat tasks the AI had already listed.

**What I couldn't check:**
- I couldn't type-check or build: the project's packages aren't installed here and downloading them was blocked.
- I haven't tested it in the running app with a real meeting.
- It only matches those phrasings. Something like "the contract's on Priya" won't be caught.
- It may sometimes add a sentence that isn't really a task. You can delete those in the meeting view.
- For very long meetings, tasks from the oldest part of the transcript (the part that gets condensed) are missed, because it only scans the transcript text still held at the end.

**Before you test again:** make sure the app is rebuilt from these files. `npm run electron:dev` rebuilds it; an app that was already running or a packaged build won't include any of these changes, including the earlier ones. That could be why the last two fixes seemed to do nothing. To confirm the new code is running, look in the terminal or log after ending a meeting for a line starting `Action-item safety net added`.

If it still looks wrong, tell me what you see: is the task missing entirely, or is it there but worded wrong or in the wrong section? And if that log line doesn't appear, the app is running an old build.
